diagnosis.observation: Every disabled task's platform updated_at followed last_run by about one minute, while the missing-role set changed across recurrences.
diagnosis.inference: The defect is strongly associated with the post-invocation/scheduler lifecycle boundary rather than a static role-id/capacity misconfiguration.
diagnosis.unverified: Whether the disable was caused by platform lifecycle behavior or a role terminal action is not yet proven.
diagnosis.next_discriminator: On recurrence, capture the exact current-control terminal receipt before re-enable. global_completion=false plus nonempty Phase-1 continuation followed by physical disable supports a platform lifecycle defect; a receipt that requests/asserts scheduler completion identifies a role terminal-contract defect.

rollback.rule: Supersede only with newer exact scheduler plus terminal-receipt evidence. Never disable a managed role, lower the denominator below 19, weaken zero-residual/zero-quota/zero-cost requirements, or mutate primary O/protected recovery.

exact_next_action: At the next run inspect current controls and live scheduler first. On any recurrence capture the disabled task's exact last_run/updated_at and current-control terminal receipt before re-enable-only repair; use that evidence to repair only the proven cause. Keep all 19 roles active and continue Phase-1 acceptance evidence.
